Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 43-year-old woman with acute onset continuous vertigo, ear buzzing, and nausea; clinical impression of labyrinthitis, started on empiric medication and advised in-person review.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden onset room-spinning dizziness for ~2 hours, associated nausea and constant ear buzzing.
- Prior episode: Similar but brief (5–10 min) one month ago, resolved spontaneously.
- Associated symptoms: Unsteady gait due to vertigo; denies limb weakness, ear pain, discharge, hearing loss, fever, recent viral illness.
- Past medical history: Premature ovarian failure; on hormone-replacement therapy (HRT).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications: HRT (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social / preventive history: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not performed in video consult.

Impression:
- Probable labyrinthitis causing acute vestibular vertigo.

Plan:
- Prescribed vertigo-control medication (name inaudible in transcript; one tablet three times daily for 10 days; dose/route not documented) to be sent to Lloyds Pharmacy.
- Arrange face-to-face appointment “in the next few days” for:
  • Otoscopic examination and assessment of gait and blood pressure.  
- Safety-net advice:
  • If new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or profuse vomiting occurs, attend Emergency Department immediately.
- Patient to phone support to book the in-person appointment.
- No dietary restrictions; medication may be taken with or without food.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements:
  – Medication name, exact dose, route.  
  – Current vitals, physical examination findings.  
  – Comprehensive medication reconciliation beyond HRT.  
  – Social history, alcohol/caffeine intake that may affect vertigo.

● Internal conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Generally clear; medication name was inaudible/omitted.
